sources.text: Recycling Right -- 1 of 13 -- Recycling Guidelines  Waste Connections uses a single stream recycling model.  All acceptable recycling materials can be placed in one container  No sorting required. -- 2 of 13 -- -- 3 of 13 -- Non-Recyclable Items  Chip Bags  Candy Wrappers  Napkins  Paper Plates  Tissues  Pizza Boxes  Plastic Grocery Bags -- 4 of 13 -- Where Your Recycling Goes?  From your home to the Recycling Center.  From the Recycling Center to the Manufacture.  From the Manufacture back to you. -- 5 of 13 -- Where Your Recycling Goes  Once your recycle has been cleaned and sorted inside your home and placed in your recycle container it is picked up by a Waste Connections recycle Truck and heads to EcoCycle. When the truck reaches EcoCycle it is put on a large conveyer belt and the sorting process starts. Plastic, paper products, metal and glass are sorted from each other. Once all the plastics have been sorted together, they are then sorted again by type. Plastic bottles used for water and soda go one way and milk containers go in another and so forth. This is done for paper, glass and metal as well. Once everything has been sorted, the different types of materials are bundled together in big cubs at a certain weight and are ready to be sold and shipped.  The cleaner the materials are the better. This allows for fewer issues with the sorting equipment and a better price. One contaminated recycle container can cause the entire truck load of material to be deemed contaminated and sends the entire load to the landfill.

sources.text: According to the EPA, here are the environmental and economic benefits of using landfill gas:  ENVIRONMENTAL BENEFITS  Landfill gas is a safe and renewable energy source.  Using landfill gas reduces the need to use more polluting forms of energy.  Using landfill gas reduces health and community risks, such as air pollution.  Landfills that use their landfill gas tend to be better managed and make better neighbors. -- 9 of 13 -- Gas to Energy Benefit BENEFITS  ECONOMIC BENEFITS  Landfill gas is a cost-effective, reliable, and local source of energy.  Using landfill gas can generate economic benefits for the community.  Developing and maintaining a landfill gas energy project creates local jobs.  A landfill with good power potential can attract business to the community. -- 10 of 13 -- Gas to Energy Benefit How It Works  According to the EPA, “When municipal solid waste is first deposited in a landfill, it undergoes an aerobic (with oxygen) decomposition stage when little methane is generated. Then, typically within less than 1 year, anaerobic conditions are established and methane-producing bacteria begin to decompose the waste and generate methane.  Landfill gas (LFG) is a natural byproduct of the decomposition of organic material in landfills. LFG is composed of roughly 50 percent methane (the primary component of natural gas), 50 percent carbon dioxide (CO2) and a small amount of non-methane organic compounds. -- 11 of 13 -- Gas to Energy Benefit How It Works  CONVERTING LANDFILL GAS TO ENERGY  Instead of escaping into the air, LFG can be captured, converted, and used as an energy source.

This system directs the collected gas to a central point where it can be transported, compressed, and filtered before it is combusted to generate electricity. -- 12 of 13 -- In Conclusion  Recycling right is the best way for Americans to protect the environment and stimulate the economy.  Recycling saves resource and reduces pollution.  Recycling is a shared responsibility.  Its easy! -- 13 of 13 --

sources.text: To learn more about WaterSense, visit www.epa.gov/watersense. 832-F-24-002 March 2024 Do This Once Per Year to Save Water:  Check your home for leaks (indoors and outdoors) and repair them promptly. Find instructions on WaterSense’s website at www.epa.gov/watersense/fix-leak-week.  Make sure your toilets aren’t continuously running. Check for leaks by putting a few drops of food coloring in the tank and wait 10 minutes; if color appears in the bowl, you have a leak. Flush afterwards to avoid staining.  Inspect showerheads and faucets for scale buildup and clean if necessary. Add new plumbing tape to ensure a tight fit.  Add mulch as needed over landscaped areas in your yard.  Check your irrigation system for breaks and leaks, signs of overwatering or underwatering, and areas of overspray, and repair or adjust as necessary. See WaterSense’s Sprinkler Spruce-Up web page at www.epa.gov/watersense/sprinklerspruce-up and Watering Tips web page at www.epa.gov/watersense/watering-tips.  Test your pool’s automatic refill system and fill valve.  Winterize your irrigation system and pool to prepare for cold weather.  Check your service water pressure and adjust or replace your pressure-regulating valve if necessary.  Have a professional service your home’s water heater and water softener (if one is installed). If you like to do it yourself, make sure to flush your water heater to reduce sediment buildup; check the water heater’s temperature and pressure valve; and clean your water softener’s brine tank. Check These Areas More Frequently for Water Waste: Daily  Turn off faucets and hose bibbs unless you are actively using water.  Run only full loads of laundry and dishes and skip extra rinse cycles.  During swim season, cover your pool when it’s not in use.

sources.text: 8155 Piney River Avenue, #150 | Littleton Colorado 80125 submit@sterlingranchdrc.com Calculating Outdoor Water Usage for a Landscape Design Every home in Sterling Ranch has an outdoor water use budget based on the overall lot square footage. For water offered at the lowest, Tier 1 billing rate, see Table 1 below. . 30% of the outdoor water budget is used by the builder for the front yard irrigation . 70% of the overall outdoor water budget remains to irrigate the backyard plants . It is recommended to not design a landscape that requires 100% of the budget to allow for seasons with high temperatures and little precipitation conditions so that the Tier 1 billing rate is not exceeded. Calculate Outdoor Water Use Determine which plants in the plan are High Water, Moderate Water, and Low Water usage. Local nursery websites are a great resource to help understand the water needs of plants. Sod, vegetable gardens, and water features are always high water usage. Then, begin calculating the irrigated square footage (sf) of the plant by using the sf of each plant at full growth. See calculations below for some typical plant sizes. Trees are the exception to the rule. As water is only delivered around the trunk of the tree, use a 3’ diameter irrigated area for calculations. -- 1 of 2 -- 8155 Piney River Avenue, #150 | Littleton Colorado 80125 submit@sterlingranchdrc.com High Water Use: plant irrigated sf x 20 gals/sf = Total gallons needed for the season Moderate Water Use: plant irrigated sf x 10 gals/sf = Total gallons needed for the season Low Water Use: plant irrigated sf x 6 gals/sf = Total gallons needed for the season For example, a Moderate Water use plant at 2’ diameter full growth: 3.142 sf irrigated area x 10 gals/sf = 31.42 gallons needed for the season.

All outdoor controlled areas must be located in the side or rear yard, abutting the home and located behind yard fencing. . May not be located in a side yard adjacent to corner sidewalk, street, common area or open space. . Must be substantially screened from view by fast-growing plant material. Evergreen plantings and grasses are required for four season screening. . Required to be kept in a clean, sanitary condition, and not allowed to fall into disrepair. Please be aware Sterling Ranch is home to various different types of wildlife. Always recommend, household pets including dogs and cats be kept indoors for their safety. Dog Run . A fenced, open-top area . May not exceed 200 square feet or more than 25% of the rear yard, whichever is less, . Constructed of fencing material matching that of lot-line fencing and stained to match lot-line fencing or may be black powder-coated steel not to exceed 48” in height from grade at any point. . Metal chain link enclosures are not permitted. . Pet mesh screen is required to be 2” x 4” galvanized welded wire mesh used on the inside of the fence, not to exceed the top rail in height, and continued down to ground level. . Covers (ex: tarps, sheets, blankets, etc.) are NOT allowed. Kennel . A free-standing panel-system kennel may not exceed 50 square feet and must be a maximum of 48 inches in height. .

sources.text: The information on this sheet is NOT all inclusive of all Community Design Guidelines or Covenants. Please review all Community governing documents prior to planning any modifications to the exterior of your home. 8220 Piney River Avenue | Littleton, Colorado 80125 | www.sterlingranchcab.com LANDSCAPE SCREENS DRC approval is required for landscape screens and will be considered based on the location of the screens, the size of your yard and the impact of screens on neighbors and the community. . 5’ maximum overall height for exposed landscape screen from grade. If plantings are installed at the base of the screen, facing out toward the community view, screen height will be allowed at a 6’ maximum overall height from grade. . 8’ maximum overall width for landscape screens. Multiple screens may not be attached at corners, at edges, to sheds, or to the house. Must be freestanding in the rear or side yard. . Landscape screens are only allowed in rear or side yards and are not allowed in easements. A maximum of three (3) screens are allowed if lot square footage permits. The DRC will review on a case by case basis. . Landscape screens must have 30% required transparency. . Materials must be constructed of a minimum 50% top grade redwood or cedar, or high grade Trex material or an equivalent in a color complementary to the home. If other materials like masonry or metal are used, they must match the architectural style of the house. Vinyl is not permitted. . Landscape screens may be either painted or stained. Paint colors must match or compliment house colors. Stain must match fence stain (Sherwin Williams #3002 Belvedere Tan) or a natural stain. Wood grain is allowed to show through. . Landscape screens may be used to screen hot tub areas on two sides only. .

Light Color: 2700K or less . Each bulb 1W or less . Light bulbs shielded or capped . Light cannot project beyond property boundaries . String lights allowed only over areas of patio or deck . sources.text: Annual Drinking Water Consumer Confidence Report: Calendar Year 2021 general information Dominion Water and Sanitation District (Dominion) is the whole sale water supplier to the CAB. Unlike other water providers, Dominion’s supply starts with renewable water. In 2021, Dominion received water through contracts with the City of Aurora. Water is diverted from the South Platte River at Strontia Springs Reservoir and then runs through the City of Aurora’s tunnel to the Rampart Reservoir and transmission pipelines to the Moore Water Treatment Plant. Once it reaches the treatment facility, a number of treatment processes are utilized including coagulation, flocculation, sedimentation, filtration and disinfection. The sources of drinking water include lakes, rivers, streams, ponds, reservoirs, springs, and wells. In order to ensure that tap water is safe to drink, Colorado Department of Health and Environment (CDPHE) prescribes regulations limiting the amount of certain contaminants in water provided by public water systems. The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations establish limits for contaminants in bottled water that must provide the same protection for public health. Results from water quality tests confirm that your drinking water complied with all EPA drinking water standards in 2021. The following information and tables represent levels of regulated and unregulated water quality parameters sampled in 2021. Note: as previously reported, our maintenance contractor had one minor violation in 2021 due to a winterized backflow preventer that was not tested in accordance with the required schedule. The concern was corrected immediately upon de-winterization and at no time was there a public safety concern.

sources.text: Health-Based − A violation of either a MCL or TT. Non-Health-Based − A violation that is not a MCL or TT. Action Level (AL) − The concentration of a contaminant which, if exceeded, triggers treatment and other regulatory requirements. Maximum Residual Disinfectant Level (MRDL) − The highest level of a disinfectant allowed in drinking water. For more information about contaminants and potential health effects, or to receive a copy of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the U.S. Centers for Disease Control (CDC) guidelines on appropriate means to lessen the risk of infection by Cryptosporidium and microbiological contaminants call the EPA Safe Drinking Water Hotline at (1-800-426-4791). The sources of drinking water (both tap water and bottled water) include rivers, lakes, streams, ponds, reservoirs, springs, and wells. As water travels over the surface of the land or through the ground, it dissolves naturally occurring minerals and, in some cases, radioactive material, and can pick up substances resulting from the presence of animals or from human activity. Contaminants that may be present in source water include: . Microbial contaminants: viruses and bacteria that may come from sewage treatment plants, septic systems, agricultural livestock operations, and wildlife. . Inorganic contaminants: salts and metals, which can be naturallyoccurring or result from urban storm water runoff, industrial or domestic wastewater discharges, oil and gas production, mining, or farming. . Pesticides and herbicides: may come from a variety of sources, such as agriculture, urban storm water runoff, and residential uses. . Radioactive contaminants: can be naturally occurring or be the result of oil and gas production and mining activities. . Organic chemical contaminants: including synthetic and volatile organic chemicals, which are byproducts of industrial processes and petroleum production, and also may come from gas stations, urban storm water runoff, and septic systems.

sources.text: In order to ensure that tap water is safe to drink, the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment prescribes regulations limiting the amount of certain contaminants in water provided by public water systems. The Food and Drug Administration regulations establish limits for contaminants in bottled water that must provide the same protection for public health. Lead in Drinking Water If present, elevated levels of lead can cause serious health problems (especially for pregnant women and young children). It is possible that lead levels at your home may be higher than other homes in the community as a result of materials used in your home’s plumbing. If you are concerned about lead in your water, you may wish to have your water tested. When your water has been sitting for several hours, you can minimize the potential for lead exposure by flushing your tap for 30 seconds to 2 minutes before using water for drinking or cooking. Additional information on lead in drinking water, testing methods, and steps you can take to minimize exposure is available from the Safe Drinking Water Hotline (1-800-426-4791) or at epa.gov/safewater/lead. Source Water Assessment and Protection (SWAP) The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment may have provided us with a Source Water Assessment Report for our water supply. For general information or to obtain a copy of the report please visit wqcdcompliance.com/ccr. The report is located under “Guidance: Source Water Assessment Reports”. Search the table using 118021, DOMINION WSD, or by contacting ANDREA COLE at 720-531-4210 . The Source Water Assessment Report provides a screening-level evaluation of potential contamination that could occur. It does not mean that the contamination has or will occur.

sources.text: Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board 2023 Annual Meeting December 12, 2023 -- 1 of 29 -- Did You Know 2123 new homes closed through December 7th with another 22 expected to be closed in December. Yep, Sterling Ranch is still the #1 in Colorado. -- 2 of 29 -- Construction Planning, design, and bidding of Prospect Park with the Resident Advisory Committee. Construction commencing in 2024 and opening in 2025. -- 3 of 29 -- -- 4 of 29 -- -- 5 of 29 -- Construction We’ve identified a location to begin due diligence for the installation of pickleball. Due diligence in 2024, budgeting for 2025 with construction early in 2025. -- 6 of 29 -- Construction The Resident Advisory Committee has identified the existing splash pad at the Overlook as an area in need of update and is working on renovations to this key amenity! -- 7 of 29 -- Construction Warranty work from contractors is managed so that roads and streets can be turned over for maintenance to Douglas County at the end of the two-year warranty period. This saves CAB taxpayers money. -- 8 of 29 -- Inspections CAB Inspectors perform quality assurance on road (asphalt and concrete), water lines, sewer lines, landscapes, and other construction activities that are public infrastructure. Those inspections ensure that the public infrastructure is built according to plans and satisfactorily. -- 9 of 29 -- Landscaping New landscapes were installed in Prospect Village tree lawns and medians (Waterton Road, Mount Ouray Road, and Monte Vista Avenue). Tree lawns along Middle Fork Avenue in Ascent Village were installed this fall. -- 10 of 29 -- Lifestyle Why do people live in a community? While there are a lot of reasons, much of it has to do with lifestyle.

sources.text: Ranch Life events have proven to be a hit and enhance the desirability and livability of Sterling Ranch. Meet your neighbors and have some fun. -- 11 of 29 -- Lifestyle -- 12 of 29 -- Welcome! Coming December 29th! -- 13 of 29 -- Weekly Ranch Life E-Blasts Keep you in the know. Don’t receive them, go to this link to sign up: -- 14 of 29 -- Funding and Saving You Money CAB secured a commitment from Douglas County to contribute $2.5 million for the construction of Prospect Park. We are grateful to our Douglas County Commissioners for their support. -- 15 of 29 -- How Do We Pay for Public Infrastructure? The CAB was created to design, acquire, construct, install, finance, operate and maintain the public improvements for the entire Community. Public improvements generally consist of street, sidewalk, alleys, water, sanitary sewer, storm sewer, park, recreation, and landscape improvements. -- 16 of 29 -- How Do We Pay for Public Infrastructure? CAB finances and pays for the construction of Public Improvements through a combination of debt instruments such as publicly sold, taxexempt, bond issuances or developer financed advances that are later converted into bonded indebtedness or paid back out of bond proceeds. -- 17 of 29 -- CAB Issued Bonds CAB DEBT FACTS: o CAB may issue debt to fund the actual capital costs of constructing public improvements as required for the phasing and build out of the entire development. o Any debt must be amortized over a period not to exceed 40 years.

sources.text: Q: Is the CAB certified to inspect the streets and other areas that they build and does Douglas County recognize our inspections? A: Inspections are carried out by both CAB personnel and Douglas County. Each entity inspects for different reasons. The CAB inspects the public infrastructure that will be owned and maintained by the CAB, for example, the water and sewer mainlines. Both the CAB team and Douglas County inspectors inspect street, curb, gutter, and sidewalk improvements that will be accepted by the County. The CAB inspects to ensure the improvements are completed to contract specification, which includes County specifications. The County inspection is additional as they are certifying their acceptance of those elements as the County has long term operations and maintenance responsibility. Q: When can we look forward to seeing Burns Park built? A: Civil construction and grading will begin in Filing 7A in early 2024. Filing 7A is the west boundary of Burns Park. As that work progresses and is completed, portions of Burns Park will begin to be constructed, starting in the southern part of the park. Very shortly CAB will be asking Douglas County for $300,000 to start designing Burns Park as a "regional park.” Q: If we have another area of homes open for development, and we need bonds to fund construction, when do those bonds need to be paid and who pays for them? A: The CAB will issue bonds to support public infrastructure construction in the new areas. That area will be part of Metropolitan District 4 Subdistrict A. CAB will issue Limited Tax General Obligation Bonds that are supported by future property tax revenues in the Subdistrict.

sources.text: As with other parts of the community, payment of those bonds is subject to the 50 mils (as adjusted) debt service mill levy cap and counts towards the total community debt limit of $1,800,000,000. Those bonds are payable only by the properties in District 4 Subdistrict-A. Other CAB debt, specifically the Jr. Subordinate bonds, are supported by the pledge of revenues from all Sterling Ranch Metropolitan Districts and pay for costs that the CAB was not able to cover at the time of construction but that benefit the entire Sterling Ranch community. -- 27 of 29 -- Q: How many schools will we have? A: Douglas County School District will continue to monitor community growth and will determine ultimately how many schools will be in Sterling Ranch. Both CAB and the School District recognize the immediate need for an elementary school here in Sterling Ranch. As many of you are aware, the most recent School District capital improvement bonds to build schools failed. Therefore, the School District doesn’t currently have the funds to build a school here in Sterling Ranch. However, there are a other options that may expedite school construction such as a charter school. Q: Who ends up paying for the bonds? A: Limited Tax General Obligation Bonds are issued by the CAB and paid for through property taxes pledged by respective districts. All debt service payments are subject to the mill levy cap and total debt issuance limitation. Q: If we can issue up to $1.8B with 12,000 homes, with interest, how much will I as an individual owner wind up paying? A: The debt authorization limit includes debt beyond the initial buildout of the community to account for refunding, refinancing, or future capital development needs.

sources.text: You’ll never pay more than the 50 mil debt service cap, as adjusted, through your taxes. What will you pay over the life of living in your home? That’s open to many different factors, including the value of your home, the length of time you live in the community, impact of future bond refunding’s and future market conditions. The bonds are paid off over 30- or 40-year increments, and the benefit of funding infrastructure through bonds is that future residents pay for the costs of improvements as well as current residents, ensuring greater equity over time. Q: Can the CAB issue bonds without an election? A: There is not a requirement for a general election prior to debt issuance. The CAB, through the Districts, has debt authorization and pledge agreements that support debt issuance. Residents elect members to serve on the Metropolitan District Boards and the District Boards appoint members to the CAB Board. Q: Regarding the school parcels, are those currently owned by Douglas County or is that land sold by the development company? A: During the land planning process, a certain amount of land is determined to be used for open space, residential, commercial, and for schools. The County requires a certain dedications at certain population thresholds. As areas of the development are platted, land is dedicated to Douglas County for specific uses, like a library or schools. The land is not sold to the County. Q: Can you talk about all the other expenses that we pay as owners, water is expensive, trash, streetlights? -- 28 of 29 -- A: Costs for these items are based on expenses. For example, the Waste Connections contract has a built-in year over year increase, and that increase is passed on to the owners for the cost of the contract. Streetlights are very similar.

The CAB was created to design, acquire, construct, install, finance, operate and maintain the public improvements for the entire Community. Public improvements generally consist of street, sidewalk, alleys, water, sanitary sewer, storm sewer, park, recreation, and landscape improvements. -- 20 of 31 -- How Do We Pay for Public Infrastructure? sources.title: Trash & Recycling
sources.text: Trash & Recycling Our trash provider is Waste Connections. Waste Connections uses automated trucks to service Sterling Ranch and provide a more efficient trash and recycling experience. The new equipment features a side arm system that makes it easier to maneuver, ensures driver safety, and allows for faster service. Trash and recycling service fees are included in your monthly CAB bill. Pick Up Schedule Make sure to place bins outside by 7 am for trash collection. Containers for pickup may be placed on the street or alleyway on the morning of pickup and must be returned to an appropriately screened location by the end of the pickup day. Please be aware Sterling Ranch is home to various types of wildlife. Pro per trash cart storage is essential to the community and its inhabitants' safety. Extra or bulky items can be picked up by contacting Waste Connections at 303-288-2100. For Providence Village , trash is picked up weekly on Monday, and recycling is picked up every other Monday. For Ascent Village, trash is picked up weekly on Tuesday, and recycling is picked up every other Tuesday. For Prospect Village , trash is picked up weekly on Thursday, and recycling is picked up every other Thursday. Holiday Schedule Trash pickup will be delayed by one day for the following holidays: New Year's Day Memorial Day Independence Day Labor Day Thanksgiving Christmas Opt-In for Service Notifications Waste Connections also has an emergency phone call system that can notify residents in case of a delay or interruption in service. Service Notification Form New Homeowners Trash Cart Delivery Trash and recycling carts will be delivered to your home within ten days of closing.

sources.title: Water & Sewer
sources.text: Water & Sewer Sterling Ranch water is provided by Dominion Water and Sanitation District, a wholesale water district serving Northwest Douglas County. To meet water demands, Dominion has contracts for permanent water delivery from Aurora Water, the Water Infrastructure and Supply Efficiency (WISE) project, and Castle Rock. Today, our water from contracts with the City of Aurora is delivered directly to the Larry D. Moore Water Treatment Plant, a facility jointly funded by Dominion and Roxborough Water and Sanitation District. Sterling Ranch: A Water-Wise Community The Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board ( CAB ) is committed to providing our residents with the highest quality tap water and reliable services. Sterling Ranch is part of a new approach to creating a regionally integrated, comprehensive water system with a robust, reliable, and renewable water supply. Dominion Water and Sanitation District and Sterling Ranch CAB have constructed a state-of-the-art water system, including a joint treatment facility with Roxborough Water and Sanitation District, the Larry D. Moore Water Treatment Plant. It is the first treatment plant in Colorado to receive 100% of its initial disinfection credits from Ultra Violet ( UV ) light and provides Sterling Ranch with clean, healthy water. Dominion Water and Sanitation District has been awarded a Certificate of Appreciation for being a WaterSense Partner by practicing and promoting water efficiency. Maintenance Checklist for a Water-Efficient Home Water & Sewer Billing After closing on their homes, Sterling Ranch residents are automatically set up for water and sewer services. Residents receive their water and sewer bills in the mail monthly and are billed in arrears.

sources.title: Water Billing
sources.text: Water Billing Sterling Ranch residents are automatically set up for water and sewer after closing on their homes. Residents receive their water and sewer bills in the mail monthly and are billed in arrears. American Conservation and Billing Solutions ( AmCoBi) administers the monthly water bill each month. Questions? AmCoBi's Client Care Services Team is available to assist you with questions or concerns regarding your water bill. Please contact them at: Toll-free: 1-833-SRCAB-40 or (833) 772-2240 E-mail: ClientCare@AmCoBi.com Payment Options: Please register your account through Utility Hawk ( https://srcab.utilityhawk.us ). Point your Web browser to: https://srcab.utilityhawk.us/login Select the "Pay Online" link on the home page. Follow the instructions. Your online account allows you to choose the best payment options for you, check your account balance and activity, and elect to receive your water bill electronically (eBill). AmCoBi's ePay service allows you to pay your bill online with an automatic withdrawal from your checking/savings account (ACH) free of charge. You can also use a debit or credit card with a processing fee of 2.95%, charged by Paymentus, the payment processing provider. Report a Water Concern If you have concerns or questions about the water in your home, please complete the Report a Water Concern Form and a staff member will be in touch with you. sources.title: Rent the Facility
sources.text: Rent the Facility The Overlook Clubhouse is an excellent venue to host your event. It provides a perfect location and a fantastic atmosphere for any occasion. The clubhouse is an ideal gathering space for organizing events, parties, community meetings, activities, picnics, groups, and clubs. The Member Services team at the Overlook Clubhouse will assist you in making your private party an event for you and your guests to remember! Great Hall The Overlook Clubhouse offers a Great Hall with a warming kitchen, an outdoor deck, and an indoor/outdoor fireplace. This space can be reserved for private use. However, when not reserved, the Great Hall, kitchen, and outdoor deck are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Please note that all members of the private rental must remain in the rented space, and additional facility access will not be permitted. Hourly Pricing $100.00 per hour with a 2-hour minimum. All rentals include the use of the indoor space and balcony. A refundable security deposit of 250.00 will also be due upon rental confirmation. Outdoor Pavilions The clubhouse has two outdoor, covered pavilions to reserve for private parties. The pavilions are available on a first-come, first-served basis when not reserved for private use. Each household can reserve one of the outdoor pavilions once per day, with no more than two rentals per calendar month. All members of the private rental must stay in the rented space. Additional facility access is not permitted. North Pavilion Larger space that includes an outdoor fireplace and convertible picnic tables South Pavilion Smaller space that includes an outdoor BBQ grill and two picnic tables Hourly Pricing $25 per hour.

sources.text: Energy Crash Course Education Program Introducing the Energy Crash Course email education series, created exclusively for Sterling Ranch residents! Learn about important energy topics and how you can reduce your energy footprint This monthly email education program was designed to give you an in-depth overview of a different residential energy topic every month for a year, making it easy for you to learn how you can do your part in helping Sterling Ranch meet our Energy Action Plan goals of: 100% renewable electricity by 2030 Carbon neutral energy supply by 2040* The purpose of the program is to make it easy for Sterling Ranch residents to get involved in our community’s Energy Action Plan by learning more about how our energy system and technologies work. As a subscriber you’ll also find opportunities to engage with the services that our community partners Copper Labs and Xcel Energy provide, and receive simple, actionable tips on how to reduce your household energy use and support renewable energy! It will be a collective effort to meet our energy goals, but this program aims to equip our community with the background knowledge necessary to feel confident in the energy actions that we make and progress together in our efforts to practice sustainable energy stewardship! SIGN UP HERE Can’t wait a whole year or want to learn at your own pace? You’re in luck! You can access every email in the Energy Crash Course series below.

sources.title: Water Billing & Payment Options
sources.text: Water Billing & Payment Options USPS Mail Pay by Check or Money Order - Send a check to the billing mailing address. All checks must be made payable to "American Conservation and Billing Solutions", P.O. Box 51280, Colorado Springs, CO 80949 Please remember to write your account number on your check . Payment Options: Please register your account through Utility Hawk ( https://srcab.utilityhawk.us ) or through the AmCoBi website: Point your Web browser to: http://www.amcobi.com/pay-online Select the "Pay Online" link on the home page. Follow the instructions. Your online account allows you to choose the best payment options for you, check your account balance and activity, and elect to receive your water bill electronically (eBill). AmCoBi's ePay service allows you to pay your bill online with an automatic withdrawal from your checking/savings account (ACH) free of charge. You can also use a debit or credit card with a processing fee of 2.95%, charged by Paymentus, the payment processing provider. Other Payment Options: Bank Bill Pay - please make sure to update your bank bill pay with your new AMCoBi account number and remittance address to ensure proper delivery. Pay by Phone at 1-833-SRCAB-40 or (833) 772-2240 Pay by Email or Text by replying to the received message from the Payment Portal. Instant Payment Options: Instant pay allows you to make a payment that AmCoBi will receive instantly using VISA, MasterCard, American Express, Discover, PayPal, Venmo, Amazon Pay, or Walmart Bill Pay. Questions? For questions about your account and general assistance, please contact the Client Care Team at AmCoBi. The AmCoBi, Colorado-based Client Care Team, will answer questions or assist with any issues that arise. They are available Monday - Friday, from 8:00 am - 5:00 pm MST.

sources.title: Understanding Your Water Bill
sources.text: Understanding Your Water Bill Sterling Ranch residents are automatically set up for water and sewer service after closing on their homes. Residents receive their water and sewer bills in the mail monthly and are billed in arrears. American Conservation and Billing Solutions ( AmCoBi) administer the monthly water bill each month. Sterling Ranch uses a tiered water rate structure for billing. This tiered water rate structure encourages water-smart usage both inside and out. The more water you use, the progressively higher rate you pay. View the tiered water rates below. What does the monthly fixed fee include? How are my indoor water usage tiers established? How do I troubleshoot your water meter when you have no water? View All /FAQ.aspx Still have questions? We have created a detailed explanation of how the tiered water billing works, with examples and tables. Understanding your water bill (pdf) Contact Us Resident Resource Center info@sterlingranchcab.com Physical Address 8220 Piney River Avenue Sterling Ranch , CO 80125 Phone: 720-661-9694 Emergency Phone: 720-661-9694 Ext. 2

It’s an all-in-one home automation, home security, and utility monitoring system that came standard with your new Sterling Ranch home. STEWARD works with voice control, smart thermostats, door locks, garage doors, security cameras, and more. sources.title: Pickleball Courts
sources.text: Pickleball Courts Pickleball Facility Guidelines Hours and Reservations Hours: Weekdays 7 am-dusk; Weekends 8 am-dusk. Courts are located at Sterling Ranch Ave. and Middle Fork St. Free street parking is available near the courts. No pets are allowed inside the courts. Courts are available for reservations and drop-in play. Courts opened for play on August 1, 2025. Court reservations can be made for a maximum of two hours/day via the Sterling Ranch CAB CourtReserve portal or CourtReserve phone app. Residents can make reservations up to seven days in advance. Non-residents can make reservations up to three days in advance starting September 1, 2025. Residents: Free Non-residents: $40/court for up to four players Open play for non-residents: $20 for two players. Open play hours: Mon-Fri: 7-11 am, 5 - 8 pm. Sat-Sun: 8-11 am, 5 - 8 pm. Reservation hours: Mon-Fri: 11 am-5 pm. Sat-Sun: 11 am-5 pm. Tournaments and lessons held by Sterling Ranch CAB take precedence. Court Reserve Court Reserve is a web-based pickleball court reservation application to make it easier for members to reserve pickleball courts, and register for open play from a web browser or phone app. Click here for details on setting up your account. General Information Follow USA Pickleball rules for behavior and etiquette. (Click here to view the rules.) Be courteous; all skill levels are welcome. Bring your own paddles and balls. Tennis or court shoes required. Courts are for pickleball only-no skateboards, bikes, pets, etc. Courts are for personal play only. Paid or private events are prohibited. CAB-organized recreational programming is allowed. No ball machines, generators, chairs, tables, or glass items on courts. Dispose of trash, avoid sitting or leaning on nets/posts. Courts may be slippery when wet.

sources.title: Design Review
sources.text: Design Review Design Review All changes to the exterior of your home or lot must to be submitted to the Design Review Committee (DRC) and written approval obtained prior to starting the work. To have your request reviewed, submit to the DRC a completed Application via email to ResidentSubmit@SterlingRanchCAB.com or dropped it off during office hours at the Resident Resource Center. The DRC may require additional information if the submitted materials do not adequately demonstrate what will be constructed. Please refer to the Governing Documents for additional information. There are consequences for failure to obtain DRC approval before making changes to the exterior of your home or lot, and for not adhering to approved plans. This includes, but is not limited to, fines, removal of unapproved materials, and/or legal actions. Design Review Committee The DRC is tasked with maintaining the visual appeal of the community, while also implementing and enforcing design guidelines that help protect and maintain property values. To that end, every resident is required to submit a completed application and obtain approval from the committee PRIOR to starting exterior modifications to your home or property. The DRC meets on the first and third Thursday of the month during March through September, and the first Thursday of the month during October through February. Design Review Timeline The DRC has up to 30 days to review a complete submittal application from the date it was RECEIVED at the DRC meeting. All submittals must be received by end of the business day on the Friday prior to a DRC meeting or else they will have to wait to be received until the following meeting date. In some cases, a fee may be a condition of the submittal.

sources.text: Streetlights Innovative Technology Sterling Ranch's intelligent streetlights use energy-efficient LED light bulbs. They come on at full illumination at dusk each evening, automatically dimming to 50% at 10:00pm and turning off automatically at sunrise each morning. These innovative streetlights still carry out the function of helping residents feel safe, but they are 70-90% more energy efficient than the regular streetlights around the state. sources.text: Court Reserve How do I create a CourtReserve account? As of July 29, 2025, the Sterling Ranch CAB has automatically created CourtReserve accounts using emails from Overlook Clubhouse memberships. If your email is in already in our Overlook Clubhouse membership database, you will have received a welcome email. Before attempting to create a new account, please check your inbox for an email from CourtReserve-your account may already be set up. Duplicate accounts cannot be created using the same email address. If you have not received a welcome email, follow the steps below. Step 1 - Visit Sterling Ranch Court Reserve Member portal and click create account. To create an acocunt click the Sterling Ranch CAB CourtReserve portal link. Step 2 - Follow the prompts to enter email, create password, and enter personal information. Step 3 - Select Resident membership type for Sterling Ranch residents. Step 4 - Once your membership is approved by CAB staff, you'll gain access to the Sterling Ranch member portal to start making reservations. Please allow 24 hours for approval.

Each household member will receive a membership card to use when entering the facility. When entering the facility, scan your card at the front desk. Guest Access Every Sterling Ranch household will receive 25 guest passes annually and is permitted to use two guest passes per day. Guests must be accompanied by a resident at all times during their use of the facility. Each household can purchase an additional 25 guest passes each year for a $100 fee. General Facility Rules & Regulations Each resident must access the facility through the front entrance. No access is permitted through pool gates or side doors of the facility. Children under the age of 13 must be accompanied by an adult over the age of 18 while using the Clubhouse or Pool. Unsupervised children will be asked to leave or to have an appropriate supervisor accompany them. All use of the fitness equipment is at the user's own risk and should be used in the proper manner. Food and drink are permitted in designated areas within the clubhouse. Adults over the age of 21 may use alcohol in permitted areas of the clubhouse. Pets are not allowed in the clubhouse or pool deck except service animals and companion animals. Proper athletic attire must be worn in the fitness facility at all times. Personal audio equipment must be contained through the use of personal headphones.

sources.text: Rules & Regulations The Community Authority Board ( CAB ) is the governing body for the Sterling Ranch. sources.title: Internet Service
sources.text: Internet Service Sterling Ranch is the first all gigabit community in Colorado, with a fiber-optic network that delivers fiber to every home. Whether you work from home or share bandwidth with the whole family, you’ll never get stuck waiting. There’s enough bandwidth for you to use technology as much - or as little - as you want. Gigabit is just the start. As residential bandwidth requirements increase, we can offer faster speeds with the infrastructure we already have in place. Quantum Fiber Partnership Lumiere has partnered with the Quantum Fiber program to deliver this powerful gig internet service to every home in Sterling Ranch. Gigabit per second speeds are included with your service, along with at least one wireless access point. The CenturyLink ON program benefits customers by providing a wireless access point, streamlined account activation, and dedicated customer service. Residents have the opportunity to add on other CenturyLink services at an additional charge. Why Fiber Internet? Fiber Internet is fast and built to last. Unlike traditional Internet infrastructure, Fiber Internet can accommodate faster speeds as technology improves, increasing the long-term value of your home! CenturyLink’s fiber network is so fast, the possibilities are nearly endless.

sources.text: Resident Services Contact Us Jessica Towles Director of Community Experience and Resident Support jessica.towles@sterlingranchcab.com Building community is Jessica’s passion - not just the building of homes but the lifestyle, camaraderie, and joy that comes when living in an active, engaged community. sources.title: Water Pressure
sources.text: Water Pressure Sterling Ranch homes have an internal PRV that needs to be periodically adjusted based on the homeowner's desired settings. The PRV (pressure-reducing valve) is inside; by adjusting it, you can get the pressures to match the street. Adjusting the PRV clockwise increases the pressure. A pressure-reducing valve is typically close to your water shutoff valve . You’ll know you’re looking at the valve because it will have a gauge nearby. Inside the valve, there are a spring and diaphragm. These two elements interact with incoming water pressure, either contracting or enlarging the hole your water ultimately passes through.

sources.title: Accessibility
sources.text: Accessibility Technology Accessibility Plan Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board "CAB" strives to ensure that its services are accessible to all residents, employees and visitors to our community. CAB has invested significant resources to help ensure that all the technology is made easier to use and more accessible for people with disabilities, with the strong belief that every person has the right to live with dignity, equality, comfort, and independence. This investment will not only help make technology accessible to users with sensory, cognitive, and mobility disabilities, but ultimately to all users, regardless of ability. A cross-functional team of caring staff members have established a committee that meets regularly to discuss how to remove accessibility barriers within the CAB technology that may affect colleagues, neighbors and visitors and work with CAB vendors to ensure solutions are being implemented. The CAB is committed to making sustained, good-faith progress on electronic accessibility to ensure that one day all will have equal access to information and services and can engage with their local government, live, work and play in this special place. The CAB has been proactively working to create technological inclusivity and continues to constantly improve the accessibility of our website, electronic content and digital services with the belief that it is our collective moral obligation to enable seamless, accessible, and unhindered use for employees and the public alike. To that end, the CAB has a plan to prioritize, evaluate, remediate and continuously improve every digital touchpoint within our services, programs, and activities.

sources.title: Accessibility
sources.text: Below, you’ll find just some of the measures that we have taken or are in the process of implementation: Remediate all agendas and minutes from July 1, 2024 through current. Review all historical documents and prioritize remediation of those documents. Sorting historical documents from remediated documents. Staff are enabling closed captioning and transcripts for public meetings held on Teams. Closed captioning is enabled via Teams for Business Meetings. Our website is regularly evaluated by an Accessibility Scanner to identify and fix accessibility barriers on our site. Web content creators are being trained on how to create accessible content for public consumption. The CAB website makes available the Website Accessibility Widget that is powered by a dedicated accessibility server through AudioEye. The software allows us to improve our website compliance with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1) level AA criteria. This is part of an ongoing effort to make all of the CAB’s technology compliant with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1) level AA criteria. The CAB website’s accessibility menu can be enabled by hitting the tab key when the page first loads or by clicking the accessibility menu icon that appears on the bottom right corner of any webpage. CAB staff are training on how to comply with OIT rules concerning accessible content. Quarterly updates are made to the CAB Technology Accessibility Inventory Assessment Tracker. Accessibility requirements have been incorporated into our technology development stages including design, development, user experience, and quality assurance. Accessibility Maturity CAB is actively engaging in addressing all technology, both internal and external facing, which is not fully accessible for all abilities.

sources.title: Accessibility
sources.text: Significant resources have been directed to this effort in terms of staff, time, effort, and financial investments. Planning efforts are being implemented enterprise-wide and implementation schedules are being developed. Organizational Measures While we’ve made progress since HB21-1110 has passed, we recognize that we are at the beginning of a long-term, on-going initiative. To that end, below are some of the steps we’ve taken to advance our position and ensure future progress: Processes will be established to provide reasonable accommodation until the technology can be made accessible. Posted an accessibility statement to the website. Historical technology not in active use will be remediated upon request. An inventory of our efforts towards compliance with the State of Colorado’s Office of Information Technology Accessibility Rules is an element of this Plan and constitutes our progress report. This plan will be reviewed annually, and the spreadsheet will be updated quarterly. This satisfies a component to be in compliance with the requirements of HB24-1454 through July 1, 2025. Identified and posted designated contact to respond to accessibility requests. sources.title: Community Authority Board
sources.text: Community Authority Board The Community Authority Board (CAB) is governed by a Board of Directors composed of representatives appointed by each participating District. Board Composition District No. 1 appoints five (5) members to the CAB Board. Districts No. 2 through No. 7 each appoint one (1) member. Each District may also appoint alternate members, who are authorized to serve in the absence or disqualification of the appointed member. Vacancies In the event of a vacancy due to term expiration, resignation, disqualification, or any other reason, the applicable District shall appoint a successor within 14 days. Meetings Regular Meetings When: Third Friday of each month at 1 pm Where: The Overlook located at 7853 Piney River Avenue, Sterling Ranch, CO 80125 and virtually Meetings are generally held in person. If a virtual option is available, access details will be included in the meeting notice posted on the CAB website. Board Members District No. 1 Representatives C. sources.title: Community Standards Committee
sources.text: Community Standards Committee Overview This committee shall be responsible for the ministerial administration and enforcement of the Documents. The CAB managing agent shall perform the tasks of Inspecting Lots, preparing correspondence regarding alleged violations, and providing other administrative support to the committee to assist with the committee's responsibilities. This committee will hold hearings and determine whether a violation has occurred and, if it has, take any enforcement action allowed by the Documents ( Resolution Formation of Enforcement Committee (PDF) ). This committee will be a 3 to 7-person committee as determined by the CAB. Meetings Community Standards Committee meetings are held on the first Tuesday of the month at 5:00 PM. The meetings are held at the Overlook Clubhouse (7853 Piney River Ave). Meetings are open to the public. sources.text: Annual Caregiver Pass Understanding that many households have caregivers that provide services for members of the household, each household can purchase an annual caregiver pass. Caregivers using the pass must be with the person they are giving care to when using the facility. One caregiver membership card will be issued per household, a list of approved caregivers must be provided. One caregiver can use the pass at each visit. Cost $300 per calendar year, no prorations permitted. Steps to Obtain an Annual Caregiver Pass Complete the Annual Caregiver Pass Form . Allow 48 hours for the Resident Services Team to process your request. You will receive a confirmation email from the Resident Services Team with instructions to pick up your caregiver pass. Payment will be due at pickup. Acceptable payment options include credit/debit card, check, and cash. sources.title: Memberships
sources.text: Memberships Resident Memberships Sterling Ranch residents can enjoy all the amazing amenities at the Overlook Clubhouse with their membership cards. There is no additional cost for club memberships for Sterling Ranch residents. It's easy to get your membership cards. Simply complete the Resident Amenity Form listing all family members and bring a copy of your closing documents to the Clubhouse. Each family member will receive a membership card to gain access to the clubhouse. Remember, a membership card (or a picture of the card) is required to enter the facility. Steps to Obtain Your Resident/Homeowner Membership Cards Once you close on your home in Sterling Ranch, complete the Resident Amenity Form . List each member of your household that lives in the house (including children). Memberships will not be given to family members not residing in the home. Proof of Sterling Ranch address will be required by all adults listed on the Resident Amenity Form that are 21 or older. Anyone 20 years of age or younger is not required proof of residency. Acceptable documentation includes closing documents, utility bills, driver's licenses, etc. You will receive a confirmation email when your membership cards are ready to be picked up from recreation@sterlingranchcab.com . Allow the Resident Services Team two business days to process your membership request and prepare your access cards. Replacement Cards Each resident requires a membership card (or a picture of your card) to access the Clubhouse. If you have lost your card, you may purchase a new one for $5.00. Guest Passes Each CAB Resident household receives 25 complimentary guest passes per calendar year.

If the Clubhouse and pool are not at capacity, additional guests beyond six (6) will be permitted for a fee of $5.00 per guest. CAB Residents are encouraged to call and verify capacity before arrival. Additional guest passes may be purchased from CAB staff and should be requested at least 48 hours in advance. Guests MUST be accompanied by the CAB Resident, who always provides guest passes while using the Clubhouse and Pool facilities. If the resident does not accompany guests, they will be asked to leave. Non-Resident Memberships Non-resident memberships are available for $850.00, up to two persons per year. There are no prorations. sources.text: Fitness Fitness Center General Facility Rules & Regulations Each resident must access the facility through the front entrance. No access is permitted through pool gates or side doors of the facility. Fitness Room Rules: Children 13 and under are prohibited from using the fitness room. Children ages 14 - 15 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian. Proper athletic attire must be worn in the fitness facility at all times. All use of the fitness equipment is at the user's own risk and should be used properly. Personal trainers may offer services with the approval of the CAB Board Wipe down all equipment after use. sources.title: Indoor Facilities
sources.text: Indoor Facilities The Overlook Clubhouse The clubhouse in Providence Village is the perfect place to gather for private parties. With indoor and outdoor space available, it is a venue for just about any occasion. Great Hall The clubhouse has a Great Hall with access to a warming kitchen, an outdoor deck, and an indoor/outdoor fireplace, and is available to reserve for private use. The Great Hall, kitchen, and outdoor deck are available on a first-come, first-served basis when not reserved. All members of the private rental must stay in the rented space; additional facility/pool access will not be permitted. Resident Hourly Fee: $100.00 per hour (two-hour minimum) Resident Refundable Security deposit: $100.00 Outdoor Pavilions The clubhouse has two outdoor, covered pavilions that are available to reserve for private parties. The pavilions are available on a first-come, first-served basis when not reserved for private use. Each household can reserve one of the outdoor pavilions once per day, with no more than two rentals per calendar month by the same resident. The pavilions cannot be rented on the same day as a Great Hall rental, unless rented in conjunction with the Great Hall. All members of the private rental must stay in the rented space; additional facility/pool access will not be permitted. Resident Hourly Fee: $25.00 per hour. Resident Refundable Security deposit: $50.00 Sterling Center The Sterling Center exhibit hall houses Atlas Coffee and Living the Dream Brewery, with a large media wall. This space is available to rent for private use for larger parties up to 200 people. The rental of this facility includes ONLY the Exhibit Hall and does not include the office section of the Sterling Center.

sources.title: Design Review Committee
sources.text: Design Review Committee Overview The application of appropriate design principles creates community goodwill and establishes visually pleasing aesthetics for all residents and visitors. With these principles in mind, the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board, through its appointed Design Review Committee, reviews and determines the acceptability of proposed changes to the exterior of your home or on your lot. Any change to the home's exterior or on the lot must be submitted to the Sterling Ranch Design Review Committee ("DRC"), and approval is obtained before any work is started. Meetings The DRC meets on the first and third Thursday of the month from March through September and the third Thursday of the month from October through February. The meetings are held at the Overlook Clubhouse (7853 Piney River Ave). Committee Members Brock Smethills Diane Smethills Rob Johnson Curtis Davidson Jason Kopecky DRC Documents, Applications and Forms Agendas & Meeting Minutes Agendas are available prior to the meetings. Minutes are available following approval. View Most Recent Agendas and Minutes

sources.title: Enforcement
sources.text: Enforcement The CAB is obligated by Community governing documents to enforce the covenants of the community. If a homeowner is not abiding by the covenants, Resident Services will take the appropriate steps to bring that property into compliance. Violation Procedure Upon notice of a regulation violation, Resident Services follows these procedures: Courtesy Notice The violation is investigated by staff and photo-documented, and notice is then sent via mail to the property owner. Each violation has a specific timeframe to "cure" or remedy. First Notice of Non-Compliance Upon re-inspection, if the violation still exists, the violation is photo-documented and the first notice of non-compliance is sent via mail to the property owner. Fine Policy Please refer to the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Code of Rules , Chapter 13, Article III, Sec 13-48 Disclosure fees. First Notice of Violation of the Documents $100.00 Second Notice of Violation of the Documents $250.00 Third Notice of Violation of the Documents $500.00 Continuing Violation Daily fines in the minimum amount of $10.00 per day An Owner who accumulates more than three (3) violations within a twelve (12) month period will be deemed to be a habitual offender. For habitual offenders, the Community Standards Committee may impose such additional fines as are deemed reasonable by the Community Standards Committee without regard to the fine schedule set forth above.

sources.text: Welcome Home On behalf of the Board of Directors and the entire Community Authority Board ("CAB"), congratulations on purchasing your new home in Sterling Ranch! The New Homeowner Guide and documents below provide information about what the CAB offers community members and a guide on "how-to's." Come on in, make yourself at home, and please let us know how we can best serve you! New Homeowner Orientation Join the CAB for a new homeowner orientation before or after your home closing. The Resident Services team will review important topics to help you get settled in, including CAB overview, mill levy and property taxes, water & sewer bills, quarterly assessments, lifestyle events and communications, amenities, design review & compliance, and a brief technology overview. New homeowner orientations are hosted monthly. Check out the upcoming schedule of New Homeowner Orientations on the Community Calendar . Follow the links to RSVP for one that is convenient for you. sources.text: Property Taxes Sterling Ranch is comprised of Sterling Ranch Metropolitan Districts 1-7. The primary purpose of the Districts is to finance the public infrastructure required by the development and to provide an ongoing governmental structure for the operation and maintenance of district improvements and facilities. Homeowners in Sterling Ranch will benefit from the construction, maintenance, repair, and replacement of the open space areas, natural areas, parks, landscaping, consistent community standards, an amenity center, and other public infrastructures in the neighborhood. These improvements and maintenance expenses are paid through homeowner property taxes collected through Douglas County in the form of a mill levy. A calculation example is provided below. sources.title: Snow Removal
sources.text: Snow Removal Snow removal is a joint effort. Douglas County handles the public roadways throughout the community. The Community Authority Board (CAB) removes snow in common areas, trails, shared drives, and alley areas. Homeowners are responsible for snow removal from their sidewalks and driveways. CAB SNOW REMOVAL Snow removal is handled by priority when the accumulation reaches the required threshold for service. Priority 1- The Overlook Clubhouse, CAB offices parking lots. Priority 2- Shared Drives, Alleys, and Mail Kiosks Priority 3- Peripheral sidewalks, parks, and areas with streets but no homes. Ice melt/sand will be applied throughout the community in areas as needed for resident safety. Minimum Threshold for Service by Area Overlook Clubhouse - zero tolerance Sidewalks - 2" threshold Mail Kiosks - 2" threshold for priority removal. Shared Drives - 2" threshold Alley Areas - 4" threshold Regional Trails - 4" threshold *Motor Courts will only be serviced by the CAB with a single plow pass when Douglas County enters its Priority Tier 3 or when the community reaches a 7" trigger. Townhomes Please contact your HOA Management Company for service questions or issues. To Best Service These Areas: Trucks will use rubber blades in all shared driveway areas. Snow will be pushed to curb stops or pulled from drives when possible. Crews will use shovels to move snow over the curb stop when possible in an effort to keep the front entryways clear. Snow markers are installed in alleys and shared drives to create the broadest possible passing lanes. Snow Hauling from shared driveway cutouts will occur on a case-by-case basis depending upon the amount of snow piled.

sources.title: Snow Removal
sources.text: When a snowstorm is predicted, please help make snow plowing easier by: No parking in back-out areas at the end of the driveways. The back-out areas are designated as NO parking areas. Removing vehicles from shared driveways, alleys, and motor courts. Storing extended downspouts in the upright position. DOUGLAS COUNTY SNOW REMOVAL Douglas County is responsible for snow removal on all public roads. Douglas County clears all roadways according to priority until conditions are safe for travel. The County only provides a single, passable lane down the middle of each street. Cul-de-sacs and some local streets may not be plowed if accumulations are minor, and snow is expected to melt over the following 24 hours. Exceptions are made if the roads have hills or curves that may become icy and hazardous to traffic. For questions or concerns related to the areas of Douglas County, please use the contact information below. When a snowstorm is in the forecast, residents are advised to move vehicles off the street if a snowstorm is forecast to allow safe access by snowplows. HOMEOWNER SNOW REMOVAL Snow and ice on sidewalks create a dangerous situation for all ages, especially for children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities who are more susceptible to injury.

sources.title: Snow Removal
sources.text: For these reasons, Douglas County Ordinance O-007-003 requires property owners in unincorporated Douglas County to remove snow and ice from the sidewalks adjacent to their property within 24 hours after it stops snowing. Direct all concerns on the homeowner responsible areas to Douglas County. Snow Placement Place all snow removed from sidewalks and driveways on your adjacent landscaped areas. This practice benefits the vegetation, reduces the amount of runoff, and helps manage the snow and ice in the street. Please do not place snow in the street. Doing so results in larger snow windrows in front of your home created by snowplows. Additionally, piles of snow in the gutter area interfere with drainage and result in buildups of ice in the gutter and on the sidewalk. Vehicle Placement When a snowstorm is predicted, remove your vehicle from the streets. During a winter storm, automobiles and other vehicles left parked on County streets, and roads make it difficult for snowplows to remove snow and ice. STERLING RANCH SNOW ANGELS If you have trouble shoveling your sidewalks and driveways, we like to offer our Sterling Ranch Snow Angels help! If you are in need of help shoveling, please email Kelsey at kstiltner@sterlingranchcab.com with your name and address. VOLUNTEER TO BE A SNOW ANGEL We are always looking for volunteers who can be called upon to help residents who cannot shovel their sidewalks and driveways after a snowstorm.

sources.title: Rachio Irrigation Controller
sources.text: Rachio Irrigation Controller Integrated with your STEWARD Start Home Automation System, the Rachio Irrigation Controller uses local weather data to optimize your outdoor watering patterns to give your yard exactly what it needs. Take the guesswork out of watering so you can water your lawn more efficiently. You’ll keep your plants healthy, use less water, and save money, while you help save the environment. Upon move-in, you will need to verify your Rachio system is running a watering schedule for your existing landscape. Getting Started Download the Rachio app to your mobile device from the App Store or Google Play Store. Log in using the username and password provided at your closing walk-through. If that login info does not work, open a support ticket Creating Watering Schedules Go to the Schedule tab in the Rachio app to see if a schedule is running on your device. For more information on creating and editing watering schedules, visit the Rachio Support Center . Technology Help Open a Support Ticket

sources.title: Ranch Life
sources.text: Ranch Life Ranch Life is all about joy! It is about bonding with your neighbors, creating lasting memories, and participating within your community. The CAB is committed to planning great events throughout the week, month, and year that positively impact your experience. Whether it be an event like a Bird Walk, Concerts in the Park, or the Cattle Drive, you have abundant opportunities to have a great time with your family while getting to know your neighbors. Ranch Life also encompasses resident-led groups. Social groups will also grow as the community grows, connecting people with similar interests. Groups can encompass anything from walking groups, book clubs, bridge clubs, and more, led by a community member. Register for Events, Programs & Fitness Offerings Visit the CIVICREC Catalog to view all upcoming events & programs.

sources.title: Clubs & Groups
sources.text: Clubs & Groups The resident-run clubs and groups are a great way for residents with similar interests to enjoy activities and hobbies together. The Overlook Clubhouse and the Sterling Center are great facilities that offer many opportunities for gatherings of different types. If you are interested in starting a club or have already started a club, contact the Lifestyle Director for more information. Please refer to the Community Calenda r for dates and any changes that may be made for the clubs and groups. Current Clubs & Groups (scroll down for full list and all-ages clubs below) Sterling Ranch BOOMER Clubs BOOMER PILATES: Offers low-impact yet highly effective exercises to increase your heart rate, mobility, and flexibility most Tuesdays and Fridays from 9:00 am - 10:00 am in the Great Room at the Overlook Clubhouse. Please bring your own yoga-type mat and water bottle. All levels are welcome. For a current schedule and more information, contact Kathy at kg3725@yahoo.com B OARD AND CARD GAMES for BOOMERS: Join other like-minded Sterling Ranch adult residents in the Great Room at the Overlook Clubhouse one Friday afternoon a month to play board and card games. Bring your favorite game to teach others, or come learn a new one. No RSVP is required. For more information, contact Astrid at astridbcarlson@gmail.com WOMEN’S BOOMER BUNCO: Join a group of fun-loving empty nesters, nearly or already retired women who play Bunco one Thursday afternoon a month in the Great Room at the Overlook Clubhouse. Bunco is a dice game that requires no strategy, just luck. Each person pays $5.00 for that day’s prizes. No RSVP is required.

sources.text: Parks & Trails Click here to view the current map of Existing Parks and Trails Trails Sterling Ranch, upon completion, will feature over 30 miles of hard and soft surface trails, ideal for local runners, walkers, birdwatchers, and bikers. Our current trails are shown in the map linked above. Community Parks Sterling Ranch is filled with beautiful parks and open spaces, encouraging residents to enjoy the great outdoors. Discover the various parks throughout the community and plan a visit. Parks Update s Click the link above for periodic updates throughout the year on our latest projects. Park Hours Parks and open spaces are open from 5 am to 11 pm daily. Parks and Open Space Rules Pets & Pet Waste Sterling Ranch is a dog-friendly community, and we want both humans and their furry companions to enjoy our outdoor amenities. If you witness any violations related to pet waste, please report them directly to Douglas County's Animal Services at 303-660-7529. Animal Services officers randomly patrol Sterling Ranch and issue tickets to pet owners who violate the rules. To ensure the safety and comfort of all residents and their pets, please follow the Douglas County Rules and Regulations listed below: As a dog owner, you are responsible for picking up and properly disposing of your dog's waste both on and off your property. There are no off-leash areas at Sterling Ranch. All dogs must be on a leash when off the owner's property. Your dog must not bite, injure, chase, threaten, bark, howl at or disturb anyone. Cats should be kept inside or, at a minimum, confined to their owner's property. To help keep our community clean, the CAB has placed pet waste stations along the trails and sidewalks throughout Sterling Ranch. Please be a good neighbor and pick up after your pets.

Motorized Vehicles Motorized vehicles are prohibited in parks, trails, and open spaces as defined in Section 12.04. Trash Glass containers, littering, dumping, and misuse of public property are prohibited. Fires Fires are permitted within charcoal-burning grills provided at park shelters or within liquid-fueled or gas-fueled grills/stoves on CAB or District-owned or managed developed park sites and parking lots when no fire restrictions apply. Firearms and Weapons Firearms are defined as any pistol, revolver, rifle, or other weapons of any description from which a shot, projectile, arrow, or bullet may be discharged. This includes and is not limited to compressed air guns, CO2 and battery-operated guns, BB guns, pellet guns, airsoft pellet guns, paintball guns, and slingshots. Archery equipment is defined as any bow including, but not limited to, a crossbow, longbow, or compound bow, which shoots arrows or other projectiles. Model rockets and airplanes are defined as any craft propelled off the ground by a gas or electric engine, CO2, compressed air, or any other form of power. Only model gliders propelled by humans and airplanes propelled by elastic bands are permitted. Possessing fireworks, firearms, archery equipment, model rockets, and airplanes on any CAB-owned or managed properties is prohibited, except as provided by Section 18-12-201, CRS, et seq. Firing or shooting any firearm or archery equipment in or into any CAB, Dominion, or District-owned or managed properties is prohibited.

sources.title: Colorado State Park Pass
sources.text: Colorado State Park Pass Experience nature at its best! We encourage you to discover all the breathtaking natural wonders that surround us by using your Colorado State Park Pass, which gives you access to the 42 State Parks in Colorado through the vehicle registration process. The State of Colorado automatically includes a State Park Pass on every vehicle registration unless the owner opts out. When you close on your home at Sterling Ranch, you will receive credit for one park pass every year, which can be renewed. This credit will allow you access to the 42 State Parks in Colorado through the vehicle registration process. One pass will be credited per household. Instructions for New Owners or Owners from Out of State Please bring proof of Sterling Ranch address to the Overlook Clubhouse to receive a voucher (closing documents, utility bill, driver’s license, etc.). Take your voucher to any state park office to redeem the annual pass to install in your vehicle. Instructions for Obtaining Your Credit Owners complete the Park Pass Reimbursement Form to submit the appropriate documentation to receive credit for their annual state park pass. Complete demographic information Upload a copy of the paid new or renewal vehicle registration Must include the Sterling Ranch address. Registration must show the park pass as paid, not opted out. Additional Passes Please note: Each household gets ONE state park pass credit or voucher. Additional passes for additional vehicles can be purchased through the vehicle registration process and will not be credited back by the CAB. If you sell your car before your park pass expires, you will need to contact the state park department for a replacement. State Park Office | 11500 N. Roxborough Park Road | Littleton, CO 80125

sources.title: Wildlife Information
sources.text: Wildlife Information Living with Wildlife "As cities along the Front Range and throughout Colorado grow, new or expanding subdivisions impact wildlife habitat. Wild animals are often displaced by development. Some species are able to live in nearby open spaces, parks, undeveloped parcels of land, river bottoms, and on or near bodies of water. Others have adapted well to urban living; skunks and raccoons, in particular, seem to thrive in and near cities. In most situations, people and wildlife can coexist. The key is to respect the wildness of wildlife. "Wildlife" is just that-wild. Most dangerous and potentially harmful encounters occur because people fail to leave the animals alone. Wildlife should not be harassed, captured, domesticated, or fed. Intentional or inadvertent feeding is the major cause of most wildlife problems, and it is illegal to feed deer, bighorn sheep, mountain goats, pronghorn, and elk in Colorado." It also has a food menu that complements your beverage of choice. With free WiFi, Atlas Coffee is ideal for remote work and studying. Atlas Coffee expanded in 2024, and is now operating as Salta (Atlas spelled backwards) after 4 pm. Offerings include an expanded food menu with several tasty options for flatbreads, a charcuterie board, and other small plates. They have also added boutique wines and cocktails for your evening enjoyment. Hours of Operation Monday - Friday: 6 am - 9 pm Saturday and Sunday: 7 am - 9 pm Online Ordering is Now Available! To place an order to pick up at your convenience, visit the Atlas Coffee website . Contact 720-767-9839

sources.title: Sterling Ranch 311
sources.text: Sterling Ranch 311 Sterling Ranch residents can use Sterling Ranch 311 to submit service requests or feedback using their mobile devices and computers. The reports will be sent directly to the appropriate Sterling Ranch CAB department(s) for follow-up and users will receive real-time updates on the CAB's progress in addressing the request. Please be advised that this request service is for non-emergency service issues, comments, and concerns only. If you're experiencing an emergency, please dial 911. To Report an Issue: Choose a service request category from the drop-down menu that matches your request. Drag the map marker to the location of your issue or type in the exact address. Click "Confirm Location". Add a photo if available or click "No Photo". Enter a description and answer any related questions. Click "Confirm Details". Download Our Mobile Apps Today!

sources.title: In Our Backyard
sources.text: In Our Backyard Life here begins with the land. Sterling Ranch is in a valley surrounded by the majestic Rocky Mountains, national parks, and open space with abundant scenic views, trails, parks, and open space to roam. Our history reflects our respect for the land and leaving the smallest imprint possible. Our deep connection to nature is reflected in our Prairie Management Plan, the preservation of our eco-system, and our water management system. This land was ranched for over 100 years and continues today In partnership with the Clough Cattle Company. Our cattle move from pasture to pasture throughout the year. This practice prevents overgrazing, aids in fire mitigation, optimizes plant regrowth, and allows the same piece of ground to be grazed multiple times during the growing season.
