sources.title: Administration
sources.text: Administration Contact Us Gary Debus General Manager gary.debus@sterlingranchcab.com Gary Debus is the General Manager for Sterling Ranch and responsible for overseeing its’ administration. Gary has a remarkable 30-year career that combines his passion for ranching and leading organizations, most notably as CEO and Community Manager for the Highlands Ranch Community Association. During his tenure, Gary led the organization in the acquisition and management of 7,500 acres of open space, constructing and managing first-class community facilities, and developing a quality of life that has earned Highlands Ranch many national rankings of the best places to live. Gary has a Bachelor of Science Degree in Mining Engineering from the Colorado School of Mines. When he’s not at Sterling Ranch, he spends time at Walking R Ranch with the love of his life, Roberta, his blue heeler, American Quarter Horses, and Black Angus cattle. Kaylin Hicks District Adminsitrator kaylin.hicks@sterlingranchcab.com As our CAB District Administrator, Kaylin serves in a key leadership role for the Sterling Ranch Metropolitan Districts (MDs) and the Community Authority Board (CAB), performing a variety of complex paralegal, administrative, professional, technical, managerial and leadership duties. She enjoys organizing, planning, and streamlining projects to ensure they are successfully completed. Prior to her career in legal administration, Kaylin began her career in event management after graduating with a bachelor’s degree from Metropolitan State University. She worked internationally for companies such as Red Robin, Noodles & Company, Valen Analytics, Tealium, ServiceNow and Lundbeck Pharmaceuticals.

sources.title: Construction
sources.text: Construction Contact Us Ed Thompson Construction Manger - Land Development Ed.Thompson@sterlingranchcab.com Ed began his career after serving in the U.S. Army, studying civil drafting, and earning degrees in Economics and Construction Management. His background includes work with civil engineering firms and real estate developers in Florida, and most recently, eight years as a Capital Improvements Project Manager for the City and County of Broomfield, managing a wide range of public infrastructure projects. Drawn to Sterling Ranch by his passion for civil, ground-up construction and creating new housing opportunities, Ed describes himself as a "YIMBY" (Yes In My Backyard) who values building great communities. Outside of work, Ed enjoys hiking, traveling, and playing basketball. He starts his mornings with coffee and a walk, and lives by the quote: "The choices we make dictate the life that we lead."

sources.title: Community Parks
sources.text: Pat Gallagher Park One of the many feature parks in Providence Village, it offers ample size yet also blends into the residences. It is located on Eagle River Loop off of the main thoroughfare, Eagle River Street. McCormick Park Located on Palmer Lake Avenue, this park's style and location are emblematic of the land use here. Flowing, contoured, and thoughtful, it combines the function and curvature of a roundabout with maximized, ample space in the center. The park is pleasantly designed for recreation and relaxation and includes a playground structure. Pioneer Park Nestled among residences on Arapahoe Peak Street, Pioneer Park is the perfect place for play and recreation. Named after Sterling Ranch's "pioneer" residents, this park includes a large grassy area and a playground structure. Children play, with parents watching from the front step or driveway, or neighbors gather at the park shelter in warm weather. Horseshoe Bend Park For all bocce ball lovers, Horseshoe Bend Park has two bocce ball courts, outdoor charcoal grills, and two park shelters. Located in Providence Village, off Horsebrush Lane and Merino Circle, the park sits amongst residences and is easily accessible by walking or biking on the trail system. Ascent Village Swan River Zipline Park As the name suggests, the ziplines here are a favorite feature for neighborhood children. This park also offers a large play structure and a covered picnic area, and is located at Swan River Street and Sterling Ranch Avenue. Animas River Park This pocket park offers permanent cornhole games and a picnic area. You can find it between Animas River Street and River Peak Circle. Basketball Park Ascent Village's Basketball Park offers a large multi-purpose turf field, picnic area, and, of course, basketball courts!

sources.title: Community Parks
sources.text: Sterling Gulch Wildlife Corridor - Ascent Village Spanning 300’ wide at its narrowest point, the Sterling Gulch Wildlife Corridor will weave through Ascent Village, connecting Providence Regional Park to the north with a larger contiguous open space to the south. It will be home to a native high plains prairie landscape and will include a grade-separated wildlife crossing underneath Waterton Road. The corridor will simultaneously balance stormwater management, residential development, and safe passage for wildlife that find their way into the corridor. Cultural Trail - Ascent Village Between the north and southbound lanes of Middle Fork Street, a typical street median suddenly widens and transforms into an unexpected open space resource facilitating physical, social, and cultural connections within Ascent Village. A trail through the center of the open space provides a vital physical connection to the larger regional trail system at Sterling Ranch. Meet some friends at the trail-head for a hike; reflect on the local art exhibits periodically staged along the trail, or just hang out and relax with a social group at one of the amenity nodes along the way. The connections are yours to discover at Ascent Village. Amenity Nodes stationed along the Cultural Trail within the Middle Fork Street Open Space will provide seating, gathering space, and other social opportunities such as bocce ball and bag-toss games. Grill out or enjoy a picnic while you await your turn to play. Stop and chat with some neighbors while on your morning walk or schedule a time to meet with your social group in this amazingly flexible space.

sources.title: Report Airplane Noise
sources.text: Report Airplane Noise Sterling Ranch and Douglas County are home to wide-open spaces. Many airplanes fly over the Sterling Ranch community and throughout Douglas County coming from the Centennial Airport. This flight pattern can sometimes cause unwanted or excessive noise. If you are concerned about airplane noise, please make sure your complaint follows the criteria below. For a Noise Complaint to be Considered Valid All noise complaints must be reported within one week of their occurrence Entering a name, phone number or email address is optional and only used for return contact if requested Any complaints made from a 3rd party medium such as a button, app or outside website will not be valid and will be discarded. Only complaints submitted via the Centennial Airport website or phone line will be accepted. Complaints must contain a residential address, time, and date at a minimum to be accepted. If a response to a complaint is desired, this must be included in the complaint filed. Complaints pertaining to aircraft that did not operate to or from Centennial Airport will not be recorded. Any complaints containing profanity or any threats to life, limb, person, or property will not be accepted and will be discarded. Submit a Noise Complaint All noise complaints can be submitted directly to the Centennial Airport for further follow-up and resolution. Report a Noise Complaint

sources.title: Help Sterling Ranch Reduce Our Energy Footprint!
sources.text: Help Sterling Ranch Reduce Our Energy Footprint! Help Sterling Ranch lead the way to a sustainable energy future Sterling Ranch is working hard to positively impact our planet by reducing its carbon footprint, without negatively impacting our residents or the cost of housing. Introducing Sterling Ranch’s Energy Action Plan Our path towards carbon neutrality is outlined in a progressive Energy Action Plan, developed through Xcel Energy’s Partners in Energy program. The plan, finalized in 2020, outlines strategies and programs to help us achieve two critical energy milestones: 100% renewable electricity by 2030 Carbon neutral energy supply by 2040* In cooperation with our residents and new home builders, here’s how we’ll get there: Residential Efficiency & Behavior Change: Reduce total energy use by connecting residents with educational opportunities and Xcel Energy programs and rebates to encourage and educate them on how to reduce their energy waste to get even more efficiency out of their already energy-efficient homes. Residential New Construction: Connect home builders with the information they need to build the most efficient, technology-ready homes by using Xcel Energy incentives which make it affordable to do so. Residential Renewables & Solar Development: Through our new Solar Made Simple program or the purchase of renewable offsets geared towards avoiding or reducing greenhouse gas emissions, we are making it easier for all Sterling Ranch residents to renewably power their homes. Attention Residents: Get Involved! Reducing your energy footprint will help your entire community! Sterling Ranch homes are already built to be extremely energy efficient, but that’s only part of the equation.

sources.title: Help Sterling Ranch Reduce Our Energy Footprint!
sources.text: For a home to truly be energy efficient, homeowners must practice energy efficient behavior. Consider taking one or more of these steps in your home: Enroll in our Energy Crash Course monthly email education program! Each email takes a deep dive into a different residential energy topic every month for a year, making it easy for Sterling Ranch residents to learn how they can take part in the Energy Action Plan. Learn More Here Look out for upcoming homeowners’ courses from the CAB and Partners in Energy to learn about how you can maximize the efficiency of your home Download the Copper Labs app and dial-in your smart home automation to reduce energy wasted on lighting, heating, and air conditioning Participate in Xcel Energy programs, like Saver’s Switch ®, to reduce peak energy demand in the summer by allowing Xcel Energy to cycle your air conditioner off and on for short 15-20 minute intervals, usually just for a few days per season. You'll get a $40 credit on your October electric bill every year you participate. How low can you go? Challenge yourself by incorporating three energy-saving tips suggested by Xcel Energy here . Ready to automate your energy savings? Check out the Xcel Energy Store for automated power strips, smart thermostats, adjustable low-flow shower heads and more, and save instantly! Once you’ve maximized your efficiency, consider taking the next step and explore your renewable energy options: Net Energy Metering allows you to get a monthly bill credit for any extra electricity you generate. All solar customers receive net-metering benefits, and in most cases, the solar developer or installer will submit an application on your behalf and manage the details of your project directly with Xcel Energy.

sources.text: Design Advisory Committee Overview The Design Advisory Committee (DAC) consists of five homeowner volunteers and one alternate who supports and advises the Design Review Committee (DRC), focusing on homeowner submissions, compliance, and improvements. The DAC will consider and review homeowner requests for impact on neighboring properties and community areas in accordance with community rules and regulations and provide the DRC with a recommendation on whether or not the DRC should approve as defined in its Documents ( Resolution Formation of Design Advisory Committee ). Meetings The DAC meets on the second and fourth Thursday of the month from March through September and the second Thursday of the month from October through February. The meetings will be held in person at the Overlook Clubhouse (7853 Piney River Ave). sources.text: Parks, Trails and Open Spaces Let's Go Explore Sterling Ranch was planned to provide abundant open space for our residents to enjoy and experience. We occupy 3,539 acres, encompassing 1,300 miles of preserved open space. More than 30% of our land is dedicated to open space, recreation, and community parks, including regional parks and pocket parks. Additionally, we have miles of bike and walking trails, so you will always find something new to explore. Trails Sterling Ranch is planned for over 30 miles of hard and soft surface trails, perfect for lo cal runners, walkers, bird watchers, and bikers. Our future trails will connect to Denver's 800-mile network. Click here to view a map of existing Parks and Trails. Parks Sterling Ranch features many parks and pocket parks - all perfect venues for events, activities and a place for kids to play and parents to connect. sources.title: In Our Backyard
sources.text: In Our Backyard Sterling Ranch is nestled in a scenic valley flanked by the Rocky Mountains to the west and two state parks, Chatfield Reservoir and Roxborough State Park, to the north and south. Explore our state parks with your Colorado State Park pass . The area boasts clear skies, making it perfect for outdoor enthusiasts. The Denver Botanic Gardens at Chatfield is located just a short distance away. The opportunities to get outside are endless. There’s a variety of trails within 20 minutes of Sterling Ranch: State Parks Chatfield State Park Roxborough State Park Trail Systems Highline Canal Trail Lyons Overlook Trail Deer Creek Canyon Park South Valley Park Golden Eagle Trail Meadowlark Trail Waterton Canyon Mary Carter Greenway Trail South Platte River Trail

sources.title: Our History
sources.text: Our History  ROOTED IN FAMILIES Sterling Ranch has been under the stewardship of only three families, all Colorado natives, for over 160 years. The Sterling Family established the ranch in the 1860s, and it was used for ranching and farming for over a century. In 1980, Frank and Joy Burns purchased the original 2,200-acre Sterling Ranch from a Denver bank. Later, in 2004, Joy Burns sold the ranch to Harold and Diane Smethills, both multi-generation Colorado natives with extensive experience in real estate, water, and business. The Smethills also bought two smaller neighboring land holdings to make Sterling Ranch the size it is today. Today, Sterling Ranch is a place for everyone. We are a large, diverse community of people from all backgrounds and ages living in single-family homes, townhouses, and apartments. Sterling Ranch is a community big enough to work and play here but small enough for people to still know each other. PLANNED FOR THE FUTURE The Smethill's vision for Sterling Ranch was to create a multi-generational, master-planned community that lived in harmony with nature, nurtured the local ecosystem, and incorporated smart technology. It took 12 years of planning to revitalize the land, create a water system, and bring smart technology to Sterling Ranch. They worked with a wide range of organizations, including neighborhood associations and many environmental groups, to achieve their goals and make Sterling Ranch what it is today, Although we are only 18% complete, Sterling Ranch is a multi-generational, eco-conscious, and SMART community that will take almost 20 years to complete. Sterling Ranch will have 12,050 homes with more than 33,000 residents on 3,500 acres with 30 miles of trails, open space, and various amenities in commercial centers.

sources.title: Chase Drain Information
sources.text: Chase Drain Information Chase Drains are a drain that is designed to collect runoff or flows originating on a private lot and facilitate transmission across County or CAB infrastructure to a gutter or storm sewer that is recessed into a sidewalk, street, alley, motor court, or shared driveway and consists of an inlet, a metal conveyance channel, a cover, and an outlet into the gutter. Douglas County has established its own policies, procedures, and guidelines under which Chase Drains may be installed in, over, or through county-owned and maintained public infrastructure to facilitate the transmission of private flows from lots to the gutter and storm drainage system. The CAB Board has established a procedure for homeowners in the community to install approved Chase Drains in CAB-owned and maintained public infrastructure in limited circumstances and where deemed necessary, and installation will not disrupt approved drainage and flow patterns. The procedures set out in this Resolution ensure that work is completed in an orderly fashion, meets engineering standards to ensure public improvements are not damaged or diminished and does not make the general public unreasonably responsible for the costs of private water flow management. Residents whose driveways face a public road are able to contact Douglas County to discuss the installation of a chase drainage system via their Report a Problem form . Residents whose driveways face a motor court, alley, or shared drive should complete the Inspection Request Form below: Chase Drain Inspection Request Form This form has been modified since it was saved.

sources.title: Bid Opportunities
sources.text: Bid Opportunities Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board (CAB) follows the public bidding process outlined for Special Districts construction projects at or above the state's statutory financial requirements. Unless otherwise noted, public bids are posted on the Dodge Construction Network. Sterling Ranch CAB is responsible for the operations and maintenance of the community. This includes performing the day-to-day activities required to maintain Sterling Ranch CAB-owned and/or maintained facilities (buildings, grounds, equipment, systems, services, and recreation) to the highest standard for the benefit of the residents and facility users. The Sterling Ranch CAB does competitive (non-public) bidding for goods, services, and maintenance valued at over $10,000. Residents and business owners that could provide one of the many goods or services (small maintenance projects, entertainment, food, event shirts, etc.) needed are encouraged to complete the form below to be added to our solicitation list. sources.title: Leak Forgiveness Policy
sources.text: Leak Forgiveness Policy In 2022, the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board passed Resolution No. 2022-11-01 regarding unintentional excessive water use. This resolution outlines the criteria that define excessive use and the relief available to residents. The following factors constitute unintentional excessive water use: The total metered use during the monthly billing cycle exceeds seven thousand five hundred (7,500) gallons. The excessive usage is not the result of an apparent deliberate act or omission of the customer such as filling a hot tub, leaving a hose running, or other intentional or controlled use of the Customer. The billing in question occurred within three (3) months. The circumstance that resulted in the unintentional excessive use has been remedied or is not subject to recurrence. The account in question is not within the "Establishment Period" for new landscape improvements. If all of the above criteria are met, Sterling Ranch CAB staff may administratively apply the following billing credit or refund to customers one (1) time within a two (2) year period: The Customer shall be billed for their average indoor or outdoor water use over the preceding 12-month period (or the CAB-wide average of users with the same meter size during a 12-month period) using CAB's standard fee schedule and applicable water tiers. The Customer shall additionally pay Tier 1 water rates for all additional gallons above the average use. This cost represents the minimum cost of treating and delivering potable water. The Customer shall pay the average sewer bill for the preceding 12-month period at the Customer's service location. The amount calculated above may be paid in one lump sum or over the subsequent two (2) billing cycles.

sources.text: Fire Mitigation Strategies Fire Mitigation in Sterling Ranch What do grazing cattle, beauty bands, concrete fencing, and community planning have in common? If you guessed "wildfire mitigation strategies", you were right! We have mulitple layers of innovative protections to help decrease the risk of wildfires in our community. Read our updated Fire Mitigation Letter, and view the Douglas Couny Wildfire Overlay Map to learn more. We recommend sending these documents to your homeowner insurance agent to help with your insurance coverage. The community continues to hold the ISO Class 1 (PPC1) Fire Rating, which is an exemplary fire rating. Sterling Ranch was featured in the news in 2025 for these strategies. Read or view the KDVR Fox 31 segment and article here . KMGH Denver 7 also reported the story ; click the link to view. View the 2025 Fire Mitigation Letter View the Douglas County Wildfire Overlay Map here. sources.title: Parks Updates
sources.text: Parks Updates Check this page for news, updates, and timelines for our ongoing parks projects in Sterling Ranch. For the most timely updates, sign up for our weekly CAB newsletters! Spring 2026: Back to Work As spring weather allows, landscape is being added to the areas around our new pickleball courts, with trees, shrubs and a few small grassy areas to help create a more park-like setting. Construction will begin this summer on Phase 2 of Prospect Park, with the new Beach Club pool! Our newest village, Parkvale, will have a fun new park; we'll share more details as work progresses. Fall 2025: Trailhead Park is coming together in Prospect Village This new pocket park is coming together at the intersection of Mount Kataka Street and Mount Ouray Road, with the landscape and hardscape completed in Fall of 2025, and a bike repair station coming soon. The park leads out into the trails and wildlife corridors along Willow Creek. Fall 2025: Pickleball Courts are now open! We have had great feedback and our residents are enjoying the new pickleball courts. Landscape is nearly complete, and we will fine tune the landscaping in Spring of 2026. Click here for details about court hours, reservations, and more . June 3, 2025: Pickleball courts in Burns Regional Park The CAB is building eight outdoor pickleball courts in Burns Regional Park, located at the southwest corner of Middle Fork Street and Sterling Ranch Avenue. We’re thrilled to share that the Douglas County Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved our request for $10.35 million to help bring Phase I of Burns Regional Park to life! sources.title: Metropolitan District Information
sources.text: Metropolitan District Information What is a Metropolitan District? A Metropolitan District is a special purpose local government, a political subdivision of the State of Colorado, and a quasi-municipal corporation created to design, fund, build, operate and maintain public infrastructure and services within its boundaries. The specific nature of the public infrastructure and services that are provided are governed by both Colorado State Statute (Title 32, Part 1 of the Colorado Revised Statutes) and the Service Plan for a Metropolitan District that is approved by either the Board of County Commissioners or City Council for the County or Municipality in which the Metropolitan District is located. A Metropolitan District is governed by a Board of Directors who are, and are elected by the, eligible electors of the District. A Metropolitan District must operate within the confines of the Constitution of the State of Colorado, Colorado statute, and the Metropolitan District’s service plan. Public Improvements and Services Provided. The Sterling Ranch Colorado Metropolitan Districts are responsible for designing, constructing, financing, installing, owning and operating the public improvements necessary to serve the Sterling Ranch community. Public improvements generally consist of street, sidewalk, alleys, water, sanitary sewer, storm sewer, park, recreation, landscape and open space improvements. Through the Community Authority Board Establishment Agreement "CABEA", the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board "CAB" was created to oversee and manage the construction and operation of the public improvements for, and on behalf of, all the Sterling Ranch Colorado Metropolitan Districts in a unified manner.

sources.title: Metropolitan District Information
sources.text: Amount of Debt The Districts Can Incur to Provide and Pay for Public Infrastructure Per the Service Plan for each Sterling Ranch Colorado Metropolitan District and the CABEA, the total amount of combined debt that may be issued, whether by the CAB or by a District, is $1,800,000,000. The total voter approved electoral debt authorization for each District is $23,400,000,000. What Revenues May Be Used to Repay Debt. Property Tax Revenues (Mill Levies) Fees and Charges, such as tap and facility fees or water and sewer service charges Other special revenues of the CAB or Districts, such as assessment lien revenues. Maximum Mill Levy it May Assess to Repay Such Debt. The District’s maximum mill levy that may be assessed for the purpose of repaying debt, including general obligation bonds, is capped at 50 mills subject to certain permissible adjustments as described below. To preserve the District’s ability to generate consistent revenue for debt service, the District Debt Mill Levy Cap may be adjusted to reflect legislative or constitutionally imposed changes in assessed valuation methodology-specifically those in effect as of January 1, 2013. These adjustments are intended to ensure that the revenue produced is not materially diminished or increased solely due to such changes. For example, a change in the ratio of actual valuation of assessable property will be considered a change in the method of calculating assessed valuation, warranting an adjustment to the mill levy cap.

Exceeding this limit would constitute a material modification of the Service Plans, requiring formal amendment procedures. Any bonds or debt obligation incurred by the CAB or a District shall be amortized over a period not to exceed forty (40) years. How a Resident Can Serve on the Board of the Metropolitan District. sources.title: Community Volunteers
sources.text: Community Volunteers Our community thrives because of the people who call Sterling Ranch home, and we’d love your help! From events and activities to special projects and community programs, there are plenty of ways to get involved. Whether you can give an hour here and there or take on a bigger role, your time and talents make a real difference. High school students can also earn credit toward their required volunteer hours for graduation. Ranch Hands Program Sometimes a little neighborly help makes all the difference! Our Ranch Hands pitch in to keep Sterling Ranch looking its best-whether it’s planting bulbs, raking leaves, or pulling those pesky weeds. Think of it as the summertime version of our Snow Angels program: instead of shovels, we bring out the rakes and gardening gloves to help those who cannot do this work themselves during a health crisis, family emergency, or other significant disruption in their life. Want to get your hands dirty (in the best way)? Sign up today and join the Ranch Hands team. Together, we’ll grow a community that’s not just connected, but rooted in kindness. Register here to volunteer as a Ranch Hand. Questions? We’re just an email away: info@sterlingranchcab.com Be a Snow Angel this Winter! When the snow starts piling up, some of our Sterling Ranch neighbors could use a little backup. That’s where our Snow Angels come in. These volunteers help clear sidewalks and driveways for those unable to shovel. It’s all about keeping our neighborhood safe, welcoming, and neighborly (and helping folks avoid slips, falls, or fines). Grab a shovel, spread some cheer, and be the reason someone smiles on a snowy day. Questions?

sources.title: How do I submit an application for Design Review?
sources.text: Question: How do I submit an application for Design Review? Answer: Please submit your completed application digitally via residentsubmit@sterlingranchcab.com Design Review Committee (DRC) meetings are scheduled for the first and third Thursday during the months of March through September, and the first Thursday during October through February. Applications and forms can be downloaded on the DRC Applications web page . Completed applications must be received via residentsubmit@sterlingranchcab.com by end of business day on the Friday prior to a DRC meeting to be reviewed at that meeting. If it is not received by end of business on the Friday before the meeting, it will be put on the following meeting’s agenda. If a fee is required, mail the physical check made out to Sterling Ranch Community Authority along with a copy of your application to Sterling Ranch DRC, 8155 Piney River Avenue, Suite 150, Littleton, CO 80125.

sources.title: How do I pay my bill?
sources.text: Question: How do I pay my bill? Answer: Water & Sewer Bill: Residents of Sterling Ranch receive a monthly water & sewer bill in the mail each month. To view and pay your monthly water & sewer bill follow the following instructions: You have on-line access to all your water and CAB Services billing information. Login to your Sterling Ranch Utility account at https://ebill.sterlingranchco.com/ubs1/ to: Pay your bill or setup an automatic payment Review your 12-month usage summary Understand your gallon consumption by month and year If you are having trouble locating your account number or need a copy of your bill please email info@sterlingranchcab.com Quarterly Assessment Bill: The quarterly CAB Service Fees are billed on a quarterly basis and are administered by Capital Consultants Management Corporation ( CCMC ). Quarterly CAB Service Fees include stormwater, trash and recycling, streetlights, and driveway maintenance (Lennar Elements homes only). Payment options are listed below. Direct-Debit The direct-debit payment option is available at no charge. If you are set up for direct-debit and your assessment has changed, the new amount will automatically be deducted. Download and complete the direct debit authorization form. Electronic Checks & Credit Card Payments To pay by Credit Card or Electronic, visit the Smartstreet Website . There is a $14.95 processing fee per credit card transaction. There is no charge for electronic check transactions. American Express, Discover, Mastercard, and Visa are accepted. Recurring credit card payments with Smartstreet are valid for one year or when your credit card expires, whichever is sooner. At that time, you must renew your payment with Smartstreet, it does not happen automatically. If you have recurring payments with Smartstreet and your assessment amount changes, you must update your payment information with Smartstreet as it doesn’t happen automatically. Bill-Payment Services If you use a bill-payment service please review your account number and payment mailing address. Many bill-payment services remit electronically and the correct account number is essential for proper posting to your account. Your account number is twelve digits with no dashes or spaces. If your assessment amount changes, you must update your bill payment processor.

sources.title: How do I register for an event or program?
sources.text: Question: How do I register for an event or program? Answer: Signing up for events, programs, and fitness offerings for your household should be easy! With the new CAB website, you’ll be able to view all upcoming events and offerings, sign up individuals in your household, and keep track of your RSVPs. After registering your household for access cards to use the Overlook Clubhouse, you will receive an email prompting you to finish your account setup. The email will read “Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board…Password Automatically Generated”. If you haven’t signed up to get access to the Overlook Clubhouse, complete the Resident Amenity Form online today! **For homeowners who registered for the Overlook Clubhouse prior to its opening in October 2020 should have received the email to complete account setup already. If you have not received the email or your link is expired, please contact the Overlook Clubhouse at 720-728-7257 or email recreation@sterlingranchcab.com and a staff member will assist you.** This account and password are for the new CIVICREC system and will be used for registering for events, reserving time to use the fitness center, purchasing fitness classes, additional guest passes, and more! Follow the instructions listed below to complete your account setup. How to Finish Your Online Account Setup Open the email. You will have a username (your email provided) and a temporary password to log in. Select TO LOGIN AND CHANGE YOUR PASSWORD NOW CLICK HERE. You will be redirected to the new CIVICREC Website. Once logged in, select ACCOUNT in the top lefthand corner. Select the pencil icon next to your name. In the lower-left corner, select RESET CIVICREC PASSWORD. You will be prompted to confirm that you would like to reset the password. A password reset link will be sent to your email. Follow the instructions to reset your password. Registering for Events & Programs Navigate to the Community Calendar . Click on the event that interests you. Click "More Details" to view the full event description, event cost, suggested ages, and registration links. Review the event details and confirm if an RSVP or program registration is required. If required, a link to register on the right-hand column will say "Register Now" Follow the registration prompts. After completing your registration, you will receive a confirmation. If you DO NOT receive a confirmation, please contact the Resident Services team ASAP. Need additional assistance? The Overlook staff is available to assist homeowners with their online accounts 7 days a week during regular business hours. If you need assistance accessing your account for the first time or if you did not receive the email to complete your account setup, please call the Overlook Clubhouse at 720-728-7257 or email recreation@sterlingranchcab.com .

sources.title: How do I trouble shoot your water meter when you have no water?
sources.text: Question: How do I trouble shoot your water meter when you have no water? Answer: Valves - Gen 1 These valves require the smart home system to be online and functioning to open and close the valves. To troubleshoot we recommend the following: Make sure the smart home system is online; if not, use https://lumiere.technology/knowledge-base/category/STEWARD/ Submit a ticket with our team at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/ Water Valves - Gen 2 These valves can easily be opened and closed manually. To troubleshoot, we recommend the following: Click the blue power button on the Dome Valve 1 time. 1 click will cause the arm to turn and open the water supply (see Gen 2 Valves #2 for that power button) If this button does not cause the arm to turn, pull the silver pin on the device and manually move the arm (see Gen 2 Valves #3 for that pin) For additional help submit a ticket at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/

sources.title: What does the monthly fixed fee include?
sources.text: Question: What does the monthly fixed fee include? Answer: The water rate billing structure includes a fixed monthly water service base fee and a residential usage charge. This base fee covers the cost of the water and sewer utility’s fixed and operating costs before any service is provided. The residential usage charge is based on tiered rates and are variable based upon use. Rates and Fees are established annually by the Community Authority Board (CAB) Board. The CAB rates are generally higher than many of the neighboring utilities and does not include a mill levy component that many neighboring utilities use to fund capital projects. However, many of these neighboring providers are older, established enterprises who rely on nonrenewable water supplies. The CAB rates are based on developing a renewable water system from inception. It is likely water rates for neighboring utilities will continue to rise at a faster rate than those of the CAB due to the costs of obtaining and developing renewable water supplies.

sources.title: How are my indoor water usage tiers established?
sources.text: Question: How are my indoor water usage tiers established? Answer: A homeowner’s individualized indoor water budget is structured on an average winter consumption ( AWC ) to determine the tier 1 threshold. The AWC is determined by averaging the customer’s actual indoor water use for the months of December, January, and February. The AWC is reset annually to allow for life changes. The tier 1 minimum threshold for residential homes is a minimum of 4,000 gallons per month and a maximum of 6,000 gallons per month. Accounts without an AWC history will be assigned 6,000 gallons per month as an initial AWC .

sources.text: Question: How do I troubleshoot your water meter when you have no water? Answer: Valves - Gen 1 These valves require the smart home system to be online and functioning to open and close the valves. To troubleshoot we recommend the following: Make sure the smart home system is online; if not, use https://lumiere.technology/knowledge-base/category/STEWARD/ Submit a ticket with our team at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/ Water Valves - Gen 2 These valves can easily be opened and closed manually. To troubleshoot, we recommend the following: Click the blue power button on the Dome Valve 1 time. 1 click will cause the arm to turn and open the water supply (see Gen 2 Valves #2 for that power button) If this button does not cause the arm to turn, pull the silver pin on the device and manually move the arm (see Gen 2 Valves #3 for that pin) For additional help submit a ticket at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/

sources.title: Why are outdoor water rates slightly higher than indoor water rates?
sources.text: Question: Why are outdoor water rates slightly higher than indoor water rates? Answer: The water rates are structured to recover system costs. Outdoor water rates were designed to encourage water-wise irrigation practices. Outdoor water use increases the demand on our water system, and therefore the operational costs of our facilities. Additionally, when water is used outdoors it is fully consumed and not returned to the system.

sources.text: Question: How do I move into higher tiers each month? Answer: The first tier of fee rates per 1,000 gallons applies to the use of up to 100% of the customer’s water budget. The tier fee rate per 1,000 gallons for use over 100% of the water budget increases based upon the amount over 100% that is used by that customer. Water used during the establishment period (45 days following the installation of turf and plant material) will be billed at the first tier fee rate, and will not count against the water budget.

sources.title: Why are you removing the virtual private network (VPN) hardware?
sources.text: Question: Why are you removing the virtual private network (VPN) hardware? Answer: The virtual private network ( VPN ) hardware was previously necessary to ensure proper encryption of water meter information during transmission to the water billing system. This is no longer the case as we are now able to use an alternate encryption method. We plan to remove the VPN hardware by default as removing it simplifies the network configuration within the home. However, if you feel strongly about keeping your VPN hardware, we will allow you to keep it.

sources.title: Can I install Automated Under Eave Lighting?
sources.text: Question: Can I install Automated Under Eave Lighting? Answer: Under-eave lighting: This type of lighting provides an architectural accent to homes and businesses. Canned lighting installed into front porch soffits/ceilings is included in this section. Architectural accent lighting includes appropriately spaced, recessed lighting strategically placed to enhance architectural elements such as columns. Architectural accent lighting shall not flash, change colors, etc. 1. Lighting must consist of hardwired fixtures installed into the soffit or hardwired track eave/rake lighting systems such as Jellyfish or Gemstone. 2. Gemstone and Jellyfish systems are the approved systems. Other similar companies/products are not permitted. a. Other companies can apply to be added to the approved list of dark sky-compliant lighting systems if they meet the following standards: • Match house trim, • Downward facing, • Limited cone of light, • As hidden as possible, • Hardwired, • Functionality to include architectural lighting options. If you have any questions or concerns about an exterior modification to your home contact the CAB staff at 720-661-9694 or via email at residentsubmit@sterlingranchcab.com PRIOR to making any changes. sources.title: What are the pool rules?
sources.text: Question: What are the pool rules? Answer: All swimmers must check in at the front desk with their membership card or a photo of it. There is no pool entrance from the side gates. Children under the age of 11 years must be accompanied and actively supervised by a parent, guardian, or if authorized by a parent/guardian, another individual of 15 years of age or older, while using the Clubhouse or Pool. Swimming any time where a lifeguard is not on duty is at the swimmer's sole risk. Lifeguards may not be on duty when temperatures are below 65 degrees and inclement weather is present. All users must take a cleansing shower before entering the pool. Showering after using the pool is recommended. Appropriate swimwear must be worn at all times. Street clothing (basketball shorts, jean/denim materials, cargo shorts), undergarments, sports bras, or similar attire is prohibited in the pool. White t-shirts or tank-tops are permitted in the pool if worn over appropriate swim attire. Pool staff will make the final determination if swimwear is appropriate. Nudity is strictly prohibited. Non-swimmers must be accompanied by a swimmer in the water and be within an arm's reach at all times. Glass containers are prohibited in the pool and pool areas. Food and beverages are permitted on the pool deck. Food and beverages are not permitted in the pool. To avoid spilling food or beverages into the pool, please keep them at your chair or table. Users who are ill, have experienced vomiting or diarrhea in the past 24 hours, have open sores, or ear/nasal discharge should not use the pool. Swim diapers must be worn by all incontinent swimmers. Horseplay, running, diving into the pool, and hanging/swinging/pulling on aquatic equipment or features is prohibited. Repeat violators will be asked to leave the pool. Lane lines, stairs, and railings are installed to assist and guide pool users. Standing, hanging from, or sitting on these items is prohibited. When lap lanes are present, those areas are for lap swimming and water walking only. During busy times, lap swimmers may be asked to share lanes, circle swim, or limit swim time to ensure all have an opportunity to use the facilities. The pool deck is reserved for walking, safety, and emergency purposes. No obstruction of any kind will be permitted in this area. Inflatable pool toys, flotation aids, or similar items are only allowed under the following conditions: Only transparent, circular inflatables no larger than 42 inches in diameter, infant inflatables, water wings with an attached chest piece, and pool noodles are permitted in the pool. Mesh infant inflatables may be no larger than 33 inches by 38 inches. Pool mattresses or other inflatables are prohibited. Users with noncompliant inflatables or flotation devices will be asked to remove them from the pool. Personal sound equipment, such as stereos or wireless speakers, are permitted as long as they do not disrupt others' enjoyment of the pool. If any complaints are received, Users will be asked to turn down their music, use headphones, or upon repeated complaint, asked to turn off the device or leave the pool. The pool must be cleared during thunder and lightning storms or other inclement weather events that present danger to Users. The pool will be cleared if lightning strikes within 10 miles of the pool, or at the discretion of Clubhouse or Pool Staff. All users must follow staff directions and safety instructions. Staff will determine when it is safe to reopen the pool. Chemicals are used to ensure a sanitary and safe water environment. Conditions are tested and documented on a regular basis. If unacceptable conditions occur, including a vomiting or fecal event, staff will determine if the pool must be closed to preserve the health, safety, and well-being of all users. Chemicals used in the pool may damage swimwear. CAB is not responsible for any such damage. CAB furniture in the pool area shall not be removed. Users may bring additional, portable lounge chairs, umbrellas, or other similar items to the pool area, provided they do not present a safety concern or unreasonably interfere with others' use and enjoyment of the pool as determined by staff.

sources.title: Can I bring a guest to the pool?
sources.text: Question: Can I bring a guest to the pool? Answer: Yes! Each household receives 25 guest passes each calendar year linked to your CIVICREC account. Each CAB Resident household is permitted up to six (6) guests per day. If the Clubhouse and Pool is not at capacity, additional guests beyond six (6) will be permitted for a fee of $5.00 per guest. CAB Residents are encouraged to call and verify capacity before arrival. Guests MUST be accompanied by the CAB Resident providing the guest passes at all times during their use of Clubhouse and Pool facilities. If guests are not accompanied by the resident, they will be asked to leave. When you arrive with your guests, please indicate the number of guest and we will deduct the passes from your account.

sources.text: Privacy Policy Types of Information We Collect: The information we gather is either information (for example, your name and address) that you voluntarily supply when you register or initiate transactions, or information gathered on usage patterns and preferences as visitors navigate the web site, use our services such as e-mail, or read our e-mail newsletters. Cookies: To help make our web site more responsive to the needs of our visitors, we use a standard feature of browser software, called a "cookie", to assign each visitor an unique, random number that resides on your computer. The cookie does not identify the visitor, just the computer that a visitor uses to access our site. Unless you voluntarily identify yourself, we won't know who you are, even if we assign a cookie to your computer as the only personal information a cookie can contain is information you supply. A cookie cannot read unrelated data off your computer. We use cookies to help us deliver a better, more personalized service. For example, we use cookies to track the pages and services on our web site visited by our users. We can build a better web site if we know which pages and features our users are visiting and how often. Browser Level Information and IP Addresses: Our web server automatically collects limited information about your computer configuration when you visit our web site, including the type of browser you use, the operating system you are running, the resolution of your computer monitor, the web site that referred you, and your IP address. Your IP address is a number that is used by computers connected to the Internet to identify your computer so that data such as the web pages you want to view can be transmitted to you.
